when: Tests whether a specified measurement model, with items assigned to constructs in advance, fits the data.
example: Theory says your twenty questions measure exactly four traits. Confirmatory factor analysis tests whether that four-trait structure actually fits the data.
small_sample: CFA usually needs 200 or more cases, so it is rarely appropriate for a small sample. Consider a shorter model or item parcels, and report any small-sample fit as tentative.
assumptions: The factor structure is specified before seeing the data
Items are continuous, or declared ordered for categorical estimation
Sample size supports stable estimation, commonly 200 or more
alternative: Exploratory factor analysis, when the structure is unknown

survey_skeleton:
# survey_skeleton.R
# StatChooser sample survey skeleton (surveyframe method = "cfa").
# Section A is a standard demographic block. Section B, and C/D/E where present,
# carry the measures the analysis plan needs. Replace every [bracketed] stem
# with your own validated items before fielding the survey.
# install.packages("surveyframe")
library(surveyframe)

# ---- Choice sets (define once, reuse) ----
agree5 <- sf_choices("agree5", 1:5,
  c("Strongly disagree", "Disagree", "Neutral", "Agree", "Strongly agree"))
gender_cs <- sf_choices("gender_cs",
  c("woman", "man", "nonbinary", "selfdescribe", "na"),
  c("Woman", "Man", "Non-binary", "Prefer to self-describe", "Prefer not to say"))
edu_cs <- sf_choices("edu_cs", 1:5,
  c("Secondary or below", "Diploma", "Bachelor degree", "Master degree", "Doctorate"))
role_cs <- sf_choices("role_cs", 1:4,
  c("Entry or junior", "Mid-level", "Senior or manager", "Executive or owner"))
industry_cs <- sf_choices("industry_cs", 1:5,
  c("Manufacturing", "Retail or trade", "Services", "Public sector", "Other"))

# ---- Section A: Respondent profile ----
sec_a <- sf_item("sec_a", "Section A: Respondent profile", type = "section_break",
  section_intro = "A few background questions about you.")
age <- sf_item("age", "Your age in years", type = "numeric")
gender <- sf_item("gender", "Your gender", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "gender_cs")
education <- sf_item("education", "Highest level of education completed", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "edu_cs")
job_role <- sf_item("job_role", "Your role or seniority", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "role_cs")
experience <- sf_item("experience", "Years of experience", type = "numeric")
industry <- sf_item("industry", "Your industry or sector", type = "single_choice", choice_set = "industry_cs")

# ---- Section B: First construct ----
sec_b <- sf_item("sec_b", "Section B: First construct", type = "section_break")
factor_1_1 <- sf_item("factor_1_1", "[Factor 1 item 1 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "factor_1")
factor_1_2 <- sf_item("factor_1_2", "[Factor 1 item 2 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "factor_1")
factor_1_3 <- sf_item("factor_1_3", "[Factor 1 item 3 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "factor_1")
factor_1 <- sf_scale("factor_1", "Factor 1", c("factor_1_1", "factor_1_2", "factor_1_3"), method = "mean")

# ---- Section C: Second construct ----
sec_c <- sf_item("sec_c", "Section C: Second construct", type = "section_break")
factor_2_1 <- sf_item("factor_2_1", "[Factor 2 item 1 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "factor_2")
factor_2_2 <- sf_item("factor_2_2", "[Factor 2 item 2 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "factor_2")
factor_2_3 <- sf_item("factor_2_3", "[Factor 2 item 3 - replace stem]", type = "likert", choice_set = "agree5", scale_id = "factor_2")
factor_2 <- sf_scale("factor_2", "Factor 2", c("factor_2_1", "factor_2_2", "factor_2_3"), method = "mean")

# ---- Assemble the instrument ----
instr <- sf_instrument(
  title         = "[Your study title]",
  description   = "[Population and purpose]",
  components    = list(
    sec_a, age, gender, education, job_role, experience, industry, sec_b, factor_1_1, factor_1_2, factor_1_3, factor_1, sec_c, factor_2_1, factor_2_2, factor_2_3, factor_2
  )
)

# Generate lavaan CFA syntax from the instrument's scales:
syntax <- cfa_lavaan_syntax(instr, ordered = TRUE)
cat(syntax)

# Fit with lavaan when ready:
# install.packages("lavaan")
